quote: Freedom is not procured by a full enjoyment of what is desired, but by controlling the desire.
author: Epictetus

quote: You must build up your life action by action, and be content if each one achieves its goal.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: No one was ever great without some portion of divine inspiration.
author: Seneca

quote: Know, first, who you are, and then adorn yourself accordingly.
author: Epictetus

quote: Ambition means tying your well-being to what other people say. Sanity means tying it to your own actions.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: True philosophy is learning to be content with what you have.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Let us say what we feel, and feel what we say; let speech harmonize with life.
author: Seneca

quote: We have the power to hold no opinion about a thing and to not let it disturb our state of mind.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Make it your goal to be like the sun: give light to all and favor to none.
author: Epictetus

quote: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
author: Seneca

quote: Your mind will take the shape of what you frequently hold in thought.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Only a fool values things by the price they are sold for.
author: Cato

quote: The comfort zone is a beautiful place, but nothing ever grows there.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: How does it help to make troubles heavier by bemoaning them?
author: Seneca

quote: People find pleasure in different things and it is my pleasure to keep my ruling faculty sound.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Certain things will grip you by the soul and demand your action. Heed these.
author: Epictetus

quote: Virtue is one; vices are many. Health is uniform; diseases are various.
author: Chrysippus

quote: Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not.
author: Epictetus

quote: No great genius has ever existed without some touch of madness.
author: Seneca

quote: Alexander the Great and his mule driver were both brought to the same place by death.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: To be even-minded is the greatest virtue. Wisdom is to speak the truth and act according to nature.
author: Zeno

quote: Mastery over the movements of the soul is the truest freedom.
author: Cleanthes

quote: The most important hour is always the present one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Fate permitting, give. If fate prevents it, endure.
author: Seneca

quote: The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: What progress have I made? I have begun to be a friend to myself.
author: Seneca

quote: Whoever is going to listen to the philosophers needs a considerable practice in listening.
author: Epictetus

quote: Take a deep breath. Do what is required of you. Don't look for credit, just do the work.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness.
author: Seneca

quote: To be calm is the highest achievement of the self.
author: Zeno

quote: Whatever happens to you has been waiting to happen since the beginning of time.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The man who has anticipated the coming of troubles takes away their power when they arrive.
author: Seneca

quote: To know that you do not know is the best. To think you know when you do not is a disease.
author: Epictetus

quote: Be like a headland of rock on which the waves break incessantly; but it stands fast.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Consider how much more you often suffer from your anger and grief than from those things that cause them.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: True wisdom consists of knowing that you know nothing.
author: Zeno

quote: The philosopher's life should be a continuous prayer.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Let virtue be the boundary of your estate, rather than gold.
author: Cato

quote: The human being who is not willing to grow is already dead.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Don't demand that things happen as you wish, but wish that they happen as they do happen.
author: Epictetus

quote: Devote the rest of your life to making progress.
author: Epictetus

quote: How ridiculous not to flee from one's own wickedness, which is possible, yet to flee from others', which is not.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Show me someone who is sick and happy, in danger and happy, dying and happy, and I'll show you a Stoic.
author: Epictetus

quote: No matter what anyone says or does, my task is to be good.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The world is maintained by the passage of one thing to another.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Whenever you are about to find fault with someone, ask yourself: what fault of mine most nearly resembles this?
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: We learn not in school, but in life.
author: Seneca

quote: Man is affected not by events but by the view he takes of them.
author: Epictetus

quote: Take pleasure in one thing and rest in it: moving from one social act to another, thinking of God.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Set aside a certain number of days, during which you shall be content with the simplest food.
author: Seneca

quote: The world is maintained by change — in the elements and in the things they compose.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
author: Seneca

quote: He has the most who is most content with the least.
author: Zeno

quote: If you are pained by any external thing, it is not the thing that disturbs you, but your own judgment about it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: True joy is a serious matter.
author: Seneca

quote: Every soul is involuntarily deprived of truth.
author: Epictetus

quote: Be steadfast as a tower that does not bend its summit before every passing wind.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The greatest wealth is a poverty of desires.
author: Seneca

quote: Man can only find meaning in his life by devoting himself to society.
author: Cleanthes

quote: If you are irritated by every rub, how will your mirror be polished?
author: Epictetus

quote: When you arise in the morning, think what a privilege it is to breathe, to think, to enjoy, to love.
author: Marcus Aurelius
